purpose: This medicine is used to lower high potassium levels in your blood, a condition called hyperkalemia. High potassium can be dangerous and cause serious heart rhythm problems. Your doctor may prescribe this if your kidneys are not removing enough potassium on their own.
how_it_works: Think of this medicine like a tiny sponge or trap inside your gut. It grabs onto extra potassium in your digestive system before it can be absorbed into your blood. The captured potassium then leaves your body naturally through your stool. This helps bring your potassium level down to a safer range.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is swelling in your legs, ankles, or feet due to fluid retention. Some people may also notice low potassium levels if the medicine works too well, so your doctor will monitor your blood levels regularly.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are on a low-sodium diet, since this medicine contains sodium and could raise your blood pressure or cause fluid buildup. It can also affect how other medicines are absorbed, so take other medications at least 2 hours before or after this medicine. Do not take it if you have a blockage in your intestines. Always keep all follow-up appointments so your potassium levels can be checked.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 10 grams taken by mouth three times a day for the first 2 days to quickly lower your potassium. After that, most people take 5 grams once a day to keep potassium levels normal. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on your blood test results. It comes as a powder that you mix with water and drink.
